topic: SGLT2 inhibitors versus GLP-1 receptor agonists in type 2 diabetes: cardiovascular and renal outcome trial results and main safety findings

key_points.point: EMPA-REG OUTCOME (7,020 patients) reduced three-point MACE by 14%, CV death by 38% and all-cause mortality by 32% versus placebo; all-cause mortality HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.57-0.82).

atoms.fact: EMPA-REG OUTCOME (7,020 patients) reduced three-point MACE by 14% versus placebo.
Empagliflozin reduced CV death by 38% and all-cause mortality by 32% in EMPA-REG OUTCOME.
All-cause mortality hazard ratio for empagliflozin was 0.68 (95% CI 0.57-0.82).

key_points.point: CANVAS (10,142 patients) reduced MACE by 14% with canagliflozin, but all-cause mortality was not significantly reduced (HR 0.87, 0.74-1.01); DECLARE-TIMI 58 (17,160) was noninferior for MACE without a significant MACE reduction (all-cause HR 0.93, 0.82-1.04).

atoms.fact: CANVAS (10,142 patients) reduced three-point MACE by 14% with canagliflozin.
Dapagliflozin in DECLARE-TIMI 58 was noninferior for MACE without a significant reduction in MACE.
All-cause mortality HR was 0.87 (0.74-1.01) for canagliflozin and 0.93 (0.82-1.04) for dapagliflozin.

key_points.point: LEADER (9,340 patients, median 3.8 years) reduced MACE from 14.9% to 13.0% (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78-0.97; p=0.01) and CV death from 6.0% to 4.7%.

atoms.fact: LEADER (9,340 patients) reduced MACE from 14.9% to 13.0% with liraglutide.
The LEADER MACE hazard ratio was 0.87 (95% CI 0.78-0.97), p=0.01 for superiority.
LEADER reduced cardiovascular death from 6.0% to 4.7%.

key_points.point: SUSTAIN-6 (3,297 patients) reduced MACE from 8.9% to 6.6% (HR 0.74, 0.58-0.95; p=0.02) and nonfatal stroke from 2.7% to 1.6% (HR 0.61, 0.38-0.99) but did not reduce CV death; retinopathy complications were higher (50 versus 29; HR 1.76, 1.11-2.78; p=0.02).

atoms.fact: SUSTAIN-6 (3,297 patients) reduced MACE from 8.9% to 6.6% (HR 0.74, 0.58-0.95).
SUSTAIN-6 reduced nonfatal stroke from 2.7% to 1.6% (HR 0.61, 0.38-0.99) but did not reduce CV death.
Retinopathy complications were higher in SUSTAIN-6, 50 versus 29 events (HR 1.76, 1.11-2.78).

key_points.point: The SGLT2 inhibitor benefit is strongest for heart failure: heart-failure hospitalisation fell 35% with empagliflozin, 33% with canagliflozin and 39% in CREDENCE; a network meta-analysis of 133 RCTs (289,558 participants) gave heart-failure RR 0.64 (0.53-0.77).

atoms.fact: Heart-failure hospitalisation was reduced by 35% with empagliflozin and 33% with canagliflozin.
A network meta-analysis of 133 RCTs found SGLT2 inhibitors reduced heart failure with RR 0.64 (0.53-0.77).
CREDENCE reduced heart-failure hospitalisation by 39%.

key_points.point: A pooled analysis of SGLT2 inhibitor CVOTs found a 45% reduction in worsening renal function, ESRD or renal death (HR 0.55, 0.48-0.64; p<0.0001); CREDENCE (4,401 patients) reduced the renal composite by 30% and DAPA-CKD gave HR 0.61 (0.51-0.72).

atoms.fact: Pooled SGLT2 CVOT data showed a 45% reduction in worsening renal function, ESRD or renal death (HR 0.55, 0.48-0.64).
CREDENCE (4,401 patients) reduced the primary renal composite by 30%.
DAPA-CKD reduced the composite renal endpoint with HR 0.61 (0.51-0.72).

key_points.point: The classes are complementary rather than interchangeable: SGLT2 inhibitors lead on heart failure and renal protection, GLP-1 receptor agonists on atherosclerotic events and weight; an indirect comparison estimated MACE HR 0.89 (0.84-0.95) for SGLT2 inhibitors and 0.82 (0.78-0.87) for GLP-1 RAs.

atoms.fact: SGLT2 inhibitors are strongest for heart failure and renal outcomes, GLP-1 receptor agonists for atherosclerotic events.
An indirect comparison estimated MACE HR 0.89 (0.84-0.95) for SGLT2 inhibitors and 0.82 (0.78-0.87) for GLP-1 receptor agonists.
A harmonised meta-analysis of eight GLP-1 CVOTs found pooled MACE HR 0.86 (0.80-0.93).

key_points.point: GLP-1 receptor agonist safety: a nonsignificant pancreatic-cancer imbalance in LEADER, nonsignificant pancreatitis and pancreatic-cancer imbalances in HARMONY, and severe hypoglycaemia 1.4% versus 0.8% with oral semaglutide in PIONEER-6.

atoms.fact: LEADER showed a nonsignificant pancreatic-cancer imbalance.
Severe hypoglycaemia was 1.4% versus 0.8% with oral semaglutide in PIONEER-6.

key_points.point: SGLT2 inhibitor safety: genital mycotic infections are more frequent (women 10.0% versus 2.6% with empagliflozin), volume depletion higher with canagliflozin (26.0% versus 18.5%), and diabetic ketoacidosis rare (56 events in 30,766 patients, 0.18%, versus 23 in 25,211, 0.09%).

atoms.fact: Genital mycotic infections were more frequent with empagliflozin, 10.0% versus 2.6% in women.
Diabetic ketoacidosis occurred in 56 of 30,766 patients (0.18%) versus 23 of 25,211 (0.09%).
Volume depletion was higher with canagliflozin, 26.0% versus 18.5%.

key_points.point: CANVAS showed increased lower-limb amputation (6.3 versus 3.4 per 1,000 patient-years) and fracture, but the amputation risk was not confirmed in CREDENCE.

atoms.fact: CANVAS showed increased lower-limb amputation, 6.3 versus 3.4 per 1,000 patient-years.
The amputation risk seen in CANVAS was not confirmed in CREDENCE.

key_points.point: GLP-1 receptor agonist renal effects are present but smaller: REWIND reduced renal outcomes from 19.6% to 17.1% (p=0.0004) and AMPLITUDE-O gave HR 0.68 (0.57-0.79).

atoms.fact: REWIND reduced renal outcomes from 19.6% to 17.1% (p=0.0004).
AMPLITUDE-O reduced renal outcomes with HR 0.68 (0.57-0.79).

key_points.point: Numbers needed to treat are not reported in these trials; only absolute event rates are available (for example LEADER 13.0% versus 14.9%, SUSTAIN-6 6.6% versus 8.9%), so any NNT must be calculated rather than quoted.

atoms.fact: These trials report absolute event rates rather than numbers needed to treat.
LEADER event rates were 13.0% versus 14.9% and SUSTAIN-6 were 6.6% versus 8.9%.
